title: The Odd noise in the roof
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：odd　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 odd 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1971 the father wrote of ① an odd noise in the roof in the letter, and everybody in the house said at once that it was ② odder than the one named there the year before. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the father, who never explained anything, had done it twice over and gone home; it was the odd ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the oddest noise in the roof anybody in the house had ever seen, or so the letter for September 1965 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too odd to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the neighbour who had come to help; the odd ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the chair at the far door, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ an odd sock under the bed, and said that no neighbour in his right mind would call it ⑥ as odd as the sock under the bed they had once had in the old house. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was odd or not, and he said so.

By 1978 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the letter. What the line asked for was ⑦ something odd, and nothing besides. The neighbour from the next house called the whole plan ⑧ quite odd; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the letter kept the names of the odd ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1981, year after year, she wrote of another odd noise in the roof in the same letter, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ odder than anybody had expected. ⑩ The oddest sock under the bed in the whole house, she said in 1983, was the one she could never quite name; the odd ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 奇怪（前置定语 an odd noise in the roof：1971 年父亲在家书里记下的那件奇怪的声响）
B. adj. 奇怪／不成对（比较级 odder than：文中两处，一处比屋顶上的奇怪声响，一处比预想）
C. adj. 奇怪／不成对（最高级 the oddest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 奇怪（表语 too odd to do：母亲觉得它太奇怪，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 不成对（前置定语 an odd sock under the bed：叔叔把整件事称作一桩不成对的袜子）
F. adj. 不成对（同级比较 as odd as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩床下单只的袜子相比）
G. adj. 不成对（后置定语 something odd：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 不成对（受程度副词修饰 quite odd：那位邻居的评价）

items.q: an odd noise in the roof
the oddest noise in the roof anybody
an odd sock under the bed
The oddest sock under the bed in

answers.why: odd 意为“奇怪”，1971 年父亲在家书里记下的是“一件奇怪的声响”，此处作前置定语 an odd noise in the roof。
odd 意为“奇怪”，此处用比较级 odder than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
odd 意为“奇怪”，家书上 九月 那行字说它是老屋里最奇怪的一件，故用最高级 the oddest noise in the roof。
odd 意为“奇怪”，母亲认为这件东西“太奇怪了，谁也用不上”，too odd to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
odd 意为“不成对”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩不成对的袜子”，此处作前置定语 an odd sock under the bed。
odd 意为“不成对”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩床下单只的袜子一样不成对”，同级比较用 as odd as。
odd 意为“不成对”，家书上那半行字要的是“不成对的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something odd。
odd 意为“不成对”，邻老屋来的那位邻居认为这套计划“相当不成对”，quite 修饰原级 odd。
odd 意为“不成对”，1981 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要不成对”，故用比较级 odder than。
odd 意为“不成对”，母亲 1983 年说的是“整个老屋里最不成对的那一桩”，故用最高级 the oddest sock under the bed。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1971 年，父亲在家书里记下了一件奇怪的声响。（an odd noise in the roof）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更奇怪。（odder than …）
母亲觉得它太奇怪，谁也用不上。（too odd to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩不成对的袜子。（an odd sock under the bed）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩床下单只的袜子一样不成对。（as odd as …）
到了 1978 年，家书上只剩半行字：要的是一件不成对的东西。（something odd）
answers: In 1971 the father wrote of an odd noise in the roof in the letter.
Everybody said it was odder than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too odd to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business an odd sock under the bed.
He said nobody would call it as odd as the sock under the bed they had once had.
By 1978 the letter asked for nothing but something odd.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 odd 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1971 the father wrote of an odd noise in the roof in the letter, and nobody forgot it.
It was the oddest noise in the roof in the house, or so the letter says.
My mother thought it too odd to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business an odd sock under the bed, and nobody argued with him.
The neighbour from the next house called the plan quite odd, and everybody laughed.
The odd ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
